opening_message:
Ticket 1: Dominic Taylor (employee ID E004) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E004.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Dominic Taylor (E004) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Source Code, owned by the Engineer role. Full-time employees may have up to write, and the role owns the system, so write is within policy.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E004 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Since training is basic, maximum is read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: HR records (the authoritative source for employment status) show E004 is a full-time Engineer. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so a full-time employee whose role owns the system is eligible up to admin; write is within policy. The requested write is granted. (Note: Security's note lists E004 as a contractor with basic training and recommends read, conflicting with HR's employment record; I rely on HR for employment status per its employee records.)
